qualification: The raw Opus, manifest, manual review and adjudication are unmodified historical receipts for exact 8b33642. They do not claim review of later battle-accuracy, metadata, building or display changes. The scoped fix and new binding tests below were performed afterward; no new browser, build or full-parity approval is claimed.
sourceEvidence: main.ts checkFrameTriggers calls frameTriggerGate.visit(String(state.map)); a new map clears the previous blocked set.
Nested source actions execute under the outer recovery checkpoint; destination entry/warp can poll frame triggers and propagate failure through the outer action.
SourceActionRecovery restores State and field before failed UI; a failed map excursion can therefore leave the live gate under a different map, or under the original map with its prior pauses erased.

The Return callback now restores a union of pre-outer and current blocked sets only when each set belongs to the restored State.map. Pauses belonging to rolled-back destination maps are excluded. This also handles an initially empty gate.
Explicit Retry still restores the exact pre-outer frame and trainer snapshots, and successful map visits retain their ordinary gate-clearing behavior.

tests.method: Node executes the actual main.ts executeSourceAction binding after stripping TypeScript, with the real SourceActionRecovery, SourceTriggerGate, TrainerAttemptLatch, ScriptVM, FieldObjects and native data; WebGL/UI ports are injected.

failures: A to B failed visit Return loses paused A
A to B to A failed excursion Return loses earlier A pause

bindingRegressions: A to B failed Return preserves original map pause and coherent save
Same-map failed Return retains newly failed trigger plus previous pauses
A to B to A failed Return unions old and new original-map pauses without destination pauses
Successful map excursions still clear pauses normally
Explicit Retry restores both pre-outer frame and trainer snapshots before replay

fullParity: Not claimed; unsupported source commands remain explicit recoverable failures.
